name: C++
title: C++ (C++11)
lifecycleNote: Replaced by C++14 and later; a current compiler accepts it as an opt-in mode.

presenceList.meta: Ec1, Ec2, Ec8, V7, L1, L2, Q1, Q4

preamble.text: Analysis against C++11 (ISO/IEC 14882:2011): threads, `std::chrono`, unordered containers, move semantics, and the smart pointers are in the standard; `std::variant` (C++17) and modules (C++20) are not. The family's C++23 page assesses the current release.

type.text: **A conversion narrows in silence**: the conversion table is a shared resource no reader is forced to hold, so a checked expression cannot be told from a narrowed one
**No sum type in the standard**: `std::variant` arrives in C++17, so a `union` plus a tag remains the encoding and every consumer re-derives which member is live
**An operator takes its meaning from the operand types**: `<<` shifts and inserts, and a reader resolves the type to know which
**A pointer may be null and the type does not say so**: each consumer writes the guard, and an omission stays invisible
**A header is the only surface, and `import` does not exist**: a module boundary arrives in C++20, so a header's declarations are all public
**A signature states no effects**: a call may write a file, mutate a global, and throw, and the signature names only the return type
**`extern "C"` is a hand-written promise**: argument order, layout, and lifetime cross a boundary that neither compiler validates

construction.text: **A binding is mutable until the code says otherwise**: `const` is opt-in, and every holder reconstructs who may write
**Placement construction separates storage from construction**: an object is built in storage the caller already holds

**The hash container ships with an unpinned order**: `std::map` keeps key order and `std::unordered_map` does not, so a program that reaches for the hash container keeps the ordering discipline itself
**One value, many names**: a pointer, a reference, a member, and a parameter reach one object, and the declaration names none of the sharers
**Execution moves with no call in sight**: a converting constructor and a conversion operator run from the contexts the standard names, not from a call the source shows
The static initialization order fiasco: namespace-scope init order across translation units is implementation-defined [@sutter1999]

memory.text: **Destructors run at scope exit**: the release is deterministic, and `unique_ptr` and `shared_ptr` put the owner in the type
**A raw pointer still names no owner**: two pointers can share one buffer with no way to say which frees it
**Storage arrives uninitialized**: default-initialization leaves scalars indeterminate, and reading one before a write is undefined behaviour
**Bytes can be read as a type they never were**: a `reinterpret_cast` and an unchecked downcast reinterpret storage with no check
**The undeclared class has no catch**: a wild pointer's trap ends the program outside every catch clause
`shared_ptr` cycles leak; the standard requires the cycle to be broken by hand

error.text: **A structured path exists**: `throw` and `catch` carry a failure from where it is raised to where it is handled
**A failure may arrive undeclared**: `throw` needs no signature entry, and no caller is required to handle it
**A failure is not an ordinary value**: nothing folds a fallible operation into an expression, so each level rebuilds the pair
**A fault ends the program**: an uncaught exception in a thread calls `std::terminate`, and the thread is not an isolation unit

concurrency.text: **Threads are in the standard**: `std::thread` runs a second computation inside the program's own structure
**Shared state is the default**: nothing marks a value thread-local or immutable
**Nothing detects a race**: the locking discipline is an agreement across files that no tool checks
**No scope joins a task**: a thread started without a scope can outlive the code that started it
**Locks, atomics, and futures are in the standard**: `std::mutex`, `std::atomic`, and `std::async` state the protocol in the source
**A concurrent task is an operating-system thread**: each task holds a thread for its whole life, and a blocked task holds one too

platform.text: **No vendor owner**: the language is standardised by ISO/IEC, and independent compilers implement it
**No required runtime**: a program compiles to native code and needs no vendor service
**Every mainstream target is supported**: compilers exist for the operating systems and embedded targets of the era

performance.text: **Compiled to native code**: no interpreter dispatch sits in the hot loop
**No collector**: release timing is the program's, not a runtime component's

ecosystem.text: **No package manager**: a dependency is resolved by a build script or by the platform's toolchain, so two checkouts can disagree about the graph
**Fragmented tooling**: the language is split across platform toolchains with different extensions and warning sets
**No cross-release binary promise**: libstdc++ documents that binaries built with one GNU release are incompatible with binaries built with another [@gccAbiPolicy]

evolution.text: **Build variants multiply**: the preprocessor's `#ifdef` tree selects which declarations reach the compiler, so a translation unit is a flag outcome
**A three-year cadence begins**: C++11 was the first feature revision after thirteen years, and the committee has shipped one every three years since
**Additive**: the revision removed almost nothing, so C++98 code compiles under it

domain.text: **Close to the machine**: the language serves systems, games, and embedded work
**Not a web or scripting language**: the work it fits least is the work it is least used for

learning.text: **Steep**: templates, multiple inheritance, manual memory, and undefined behaviour build on nothing a mainstream background supplies
**Several paradigms at once**: procedural, object-oriented, and generic code all remain available for the same task
**An authoritative standard text and a large literature**: the reference is public and complete

syntax.text: **Nested instantiations tax the reader**: a template argument can itself be an instantiation, and the reader unfolds the chain to know the type it produces
**Declarations state types once**: the reader resolves a type at its declaration rather than at each use

testing.text: **Testing arrives from outside the toolchain**: `assert` is in the library and no runner is, so a framework and a runner are adopted per project
**A mature debugger exists for every platform**: the toolchain is the platform's, and it steps through the source
**A monotonic clock is in the standard**: `std::chrono::steady_clock` publishes an elapsed reading that the program can call

security.text: **Memory-unsafe**: a buffer overflow, a use-after-free, and a double free all compile, and any pointer suffices
The inherited C rule: signed overflow undefined, unsigned modulo; the optimizer exploits both

reproducibility.text: **Builds are not byte-reproducible by default**: timestamps and absolute paths reach the artifact, so a third party cannot confirm it matches the source

supplychain.text: **No registry, so no signed provenance**: a dependency is a source tree or a library, and its origin is taken on trust

feedback.text: **A change pays a slow build**: templates and a long link step sit on the critical path of every edit

interop.text: **A general foreign-function interface exists**: the platform's C ABI is the boundary, and the language calls it directly

governance.text: **An open standard with no conformance suite**: the standard lists implementation-defined behaviour, and the committee publishes no suite an independent implementation runs

observability.text: **A failure leaves no post-mortem by default**: without a debugger and an enabled core dump, an unhandled failure prints nothing

tradeoffs: **Zero-cost abstraction vs. reading time**: templates and inline code remove runtime cost and add ceremony at every declaration
**Placement construction vs. readability**: building an object in storage the caller chose is a precise control, and the reader reconstructs where that storage came from
verdict: C++11 is the revision that put concurrency, ownership transfer, and a monotonic clock into the language. `std::thread`, `std::mutex`, and `std::atomic` answer the missing coordination primitives. Move semantics and the smart pointers state an owner that raw pointers never named. Unordered containers arrive: the hash container's iteration order becomes something a program must not rely on, while `std::map` keeps key order. What the standard still does not provide: a sum type (C++17), a module boundary (C++20), and a composable failure value (C++23). Main strength: the era's most complete zero-overhead toolkit. Main weakness: raw pointers, unchecked casts, and the preprocessor remain, so the guarantees depend on idiom.

energy.text: Compiles to native code: the fastest class in the language energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy; @pereira2021ranking]. A causal re-analysis attributes the difference to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: A large training corpus and strong code-generation results: models write this language well [@joel2025lowresource; @effibenchx2025].

safety.text: A standards-qualified toolchain or an established safety standard covers this language.

delivery.note: A recipe builds from source on the consumer machine
libstdc++ documents that binaries built with one GNU release are incompatible with binaries built with another, and mixing C++ ABIs is not recommended
